ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Statistical Thinking in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology. This seminar/workshop will focus on the process of translating biological understanding into statistical models. This course is aimed at "mid-career" graduate students who have had some formal training in statistics and have collected or will soon start collecting their own data, and will use the student's own data sets to explore both philosophical (why is this class of model the best way to represent this particular dataset?) and practical (fitting the model and interpreting the results, dealing with imperfect data, etc.) issues. Specific topics will be driven by student interest, but are likely to include general and generalized linear models, random effects and mixed models, multivariate and ordination approaches, information theoretic approaches, and others.
